about: Per-part syllabus tags for AI HL. Codes are the AI guide's own numbers (data/syllabus-ai.json); statements AI shares with AA keep AA's sub-tag ids. Each part was tagged by two independent blind reviewers; parts where they disagreed were settled by an adjudicator (review: adjudicated, with rationale and both original tag sets). HL appearances of SL questions (data/shared.json) take the SL tags and are not listed here.

parts.skill: State the independence assumption behind a binomial test of a proportion.

parts.label: c(ii)
parts.skill: Set n from the totals and find an upper-tail binomial p-value.

parts.label: c(iii)
parts.skill: Compare the binomial p-value with the significance level and conclude.

parts.label: d(i)
parts.skill: Write independence hypotheses for a contingency-table test in context.

parts.label: d(ii)
parts.skill: Obtain the chi-squared independence p-value and show it is not significant.

parts.label: e
parts.skill: Form differences, state hypotheses on the mean difference, run a one-tailed paired t-test and conclude.

parts.label: f
parts.skill: Draw a justified overall conclusion about home advantage by weighing the results of more than one of the earlier tests.

parts.label: a(i)
parts.skill: Justify a quadratic model from the down-then-up shape of the scatter.

parts.label: a(ii)
parts.skill: Fit a least squares quadratic regression with technology.

parts.label: b
parts.skill: Explain that the quadratic grows without bound while the real temperature levels off.

parts.label: c
parts.skill: Use the initial condition to fix the constant in the model.

parts.label: d(i)
parts.skill: Differentiate a product of a fractional power and an exponential.

parts.label: d(ii)
parts.skill: Set the derivative to zero at the given minimum and eliminate the other factors to find the parameter.
parts.rationale: After 'hence' the derivative is reused, so the marks are for using f'(16) = 0 at a known minimum to find an unknown constant (5.6); no new differentiation (5.9) or separate fitting step (2.6) earns marks.

parts.label: d(iii)
parts.skill: Substitute the minimum point and known parameters to solve for the remaining one.

parts.label: d(iv)
parts.skill: Assemble the fitted model from the parameters found.

parts.label: e
parts.skill: Compute a transformed data value from the given rearrangement.

parts.label: f(i)
parts.skill: Take logs of the transformed values and fit a linear regression of ln x on t.

parts.label: f(ii)
parts.skill: Match the regression line for ln x to ln a - bt and undo the log to recover a and b.

parts.label: f(iii)
parts.skill: Write the full temperature model using the parameters from the linearised fit.

parts.label: g(i)
parts.skill: Identify the quadratic model's graph from its parabolic, symmetric shape or its y-intercept.
parts.rationale: The A1 is for matching a model to its graph (2.3) and the R1 for justifying it by the quadratic's own features (2.5); it does not test the model against data, so 2.6 does not fit.

parts.label: g(ii)
parts.skill: Pick the regression model's curve, reasoning that least squares minimises the sum of square residuals while the other model is forced through the minimum.
parts.rationale: The R1 is an SSres argument comparing two fitted models, which the 2.6 line sends to 4.13, and the A1 is for matching the model to its graph (2.3).
